recommendation: GoatCounter hosted: free for reasonable public usage, open source, cookie-free visit counting, per-article RSS image endpoint without creating a pixel manually for every article.

platforms.name: GoatCounter
platforms.cost: Free hosted for reasonable public usage; donations optional. Self-hosting also available.
platforms.fit: Recommended for this personal site and RSS image loads.

platforms.name: Umami Cloud
platforms.cost: Hobby: free, one website, 100,000 events/month, 6 months retention. Pro: $20/month.
platforms.fit: Good free alternative. Version 3 supports tracking pixels created through its dashboard; confirm plan-specific pixel quotas before choosing.

platforms.name: Plausible
platforms.cost: Starter: $9/month for up to 10,000 monthly pageviews, one site; annual billing discount.
platforms.fit: Good paid option with EU hosting. The documented Events API requires POST; an RSS img GET would need a separate collector/bridge.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Web Analytics
platforms.fit: Browser traffic and performance; JavaScript beacon works on GitHub Pages without changing DNS. Not a drop-in RSS tracking-image service.

platforms.name: Simple Analytics
platforms.cost: Free hobby tier: 5 sites, one user, 1 month history, visible badge required.
platforms.fit: Short retention and required badge make it less suitable here.

feed_findings.duplicate: Autodiscovery advertised /rss.xml/ (404); footer advertised /rss.xml (200). Only one feed generator exists. Both now use /rss.xml, with an Atom self-link inside the RSS feed, not a second Atom feed.
feed_findings.content: Full rendered HTML is sanitized, links and image URLs made absolute. Original item GUIDs preserved. pubDate uses original publication date rather than revision date.

integration.status: Enabled for production builds with https://marcprux.goatcounter.com/count, supplied by Marc on 2026-10-28. Requires Marc to commit/push and the existing GitHub Pages deployment to complete.
integration.configuration: Configured in src/analytics.config.ts. No API key or GitHub secret required. Dashboard: https://marcprux.goatcounter.com/user/dashboard.
integration.browser: Production only. Tracks completed Astro page loads. Path omits query strings and fragments. A noscript 1x1 image provides a fallback without counting twice for JavaScript users.
integration.rss: One invisible 1x1 image per article, with p=/rss/posts/<slug>/ and the article title. Unique per article, not per person. No subscriber identifiers.
integration.preview: Dev mode emits no tracking script or pixels. Production JS also checks the deployed hostname; no-JavaScript production previews and opened production RSS exports still contain the live pixel URLs once configured.
integration.metrics: Browser page visits and /rss/ image-load visits are separate. Image caching/proxying/blocking/preloading and bots mean RSS loads cannot establish exact readership or completed reads. Do not add the two channels together as unique people.

limitations: Hosted GitHub Pages cannot implement a dynamic image-counting endpoint itself; analytics needs an external collector or separately hosted service.
No historical visitor counts can be recovered from adding this integration now.
GoatCounter deduplicates visits using site/IP/User-Agent held in memory for up to eight hours; it is not identity-based counting.
validation: Production build and Astro check pass.
Enabled integration tested against a synthetic .invalid endpoint in a temporary build, with no requests sent to an analytics service.
All five RSS items match full website article text, keep existing GUIDs, contain no scripts, and use absolute links.
One canonical RSS discovery link per generated page.
Enabled RSS includes exactly one distinct pixel per article.
Tracker initialization tested with early and late script load, initial load, client navigation/back, repeat setup, and local host exclusion.

Production build verified with Marc’s real endpoint and five distinct RSS article pixels; homepage, article, and RSS development previews contain no tracking. No synthetic visits sent to the live collector.
